test.title: Learning to cycle in the city

paragraphs.text: Adult cycling courses fill up within hours in most cities. Half of those who sign up can already ride but are afraid of traffic; the rest have never sat on a bicycle.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Instructors start on quiet streets and teach riders to look behind without wobbling, which most people find harder than braking. Roundabouts are left until the last lesson.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A year later, two thirds of those who finished the course still ride at least once a week, and most of them say they would not go back to the bus.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Courses do not solve everything. Where a city has no protected lanes, confidence fades within months, and riders return to the pavement or stop altogether.
paragraphs.label: D
